You can acquire the cathedral shard by heading south-west to a courtyard full of Zamorakian acolytes and mages and, using your mithril (or above) logging axe, cut down the vines. As the mages and acolytes are hostile by default, you will need to take them down first.

He is located underground in The Garrison region, protected by two hellhounds and a small host of skeletons. The requirements to interact/collect this shard are the same as defeating the shardbound lesser demons.

Navigate past the elite Black Knight and two Zamorakian acolytes to an open wall with some wooden boards. Use the Windstep spell to jump up and across to the nearby adjacent tower. Once you have arrived, either defeat or avoid the elite Black Knight to interact with the shard.
Spittletoe instructs you to collect five Maple Sap. Once you provide the sap, Spittletoe will trade you the shard.

Speak with Spittletoe Speak with Spittletoe, while having the maple sap in your inventory. Continue dialogue until you receive a shard. Note: When interacting with Spittletoe in the kitchen, it is possible for the Zogre to aggro the player from above, even without being in line of sight.[uncheck all] If you do not have the maple sap, look for maple trees and chop them down till you get one

Open the library door by interacting with (in order) the following books: The Empty Throne The Eye of Oculus Taking the Crown Zamorak's Rebellion Note: You can make it easier to take them down by leading them up the spiral staircase. Despite the player needing to interact with the doorway to phase through, the lesser demons can't walk through, allowing them to be attacked with ranged from behind the door.

Go to the top of the staircase (a floor above where Valerius can be found) and West, past the blue dragon, and veer right as soon as you pass under the cliff. Equip your spade and dig in front of the gargoyle statue to uncover the glass owl. Return this item to Valerius to acquire this shard.
Dig with spade Cut down vines w/ mithril logging axe

Find three levers to unlock the door. The first lever is inside of the broken down roof of the tiny house (located next to the windmill). You'll need to cast Windstep to reach the roof, then use your spade here to dig it up and interact with it. The second lever is inside of a cave nearby protected by a thorny vine wall along the rock wall to the right of the shard. You will need a mithril or better logging axe to chop these vines. The third and final lever is on the top level of the nearby stone ruins, located beside the air anima vent. You'll need to use Windstep to reach this level. This area is guarded by a lesser blue dragon.

Follow along the lower area cliffs to reach an area where you can jump across. You'll also locate a group of hellhounds on your way there, but you can either ignore them or defeat them until you locate a series of beams. Traverse the beams by jumping up to the next level until you reach the top where you'll need to jump across to the stone rock where the shard is located. Note: You'll need plenty of air runes to use Windstep for this particular jumping puzzle. An alternative way is to equip your leggings of lightness and use Windstep from where you received the previous shard from finding the three levers, down to the cliffs. Be sure not to jump and head down, instead, fall with the spell and the leggings to avoid damage.

Reach the highest part of the goblin-infested fortress. In the middle of the area, there is a granite deposit that hides the shard. You can either avoid or defeat the blue dragon here to get to the shard, but you can use the Rocksplosion spell to quickly interact with the shard.
Defeat the goblins in the immediate area of the shard before interacting with it.

Navigate to The Crypt in the underground region. Before searching for the shard, defeat the zogre here. This will save you trouble later. Interact with the note next to the goblin corpse to learn that the shard is buried in a grave. Dig at any of the graves until you uncover the shard. Note: The location of this shard is randomized for every world.

Navigate to the lowest part of the region. There is a lever-activated elevator that will take you down to the demon gate region. For easier traversal later, interact with the nearby nodestone to connect it to the Nexus. Navigate through the pathways until you reach the stone structure and defeat the two lesser demons guarding the shard.

He will ask you to give him one of the fish nearby (requires an empty inventory slot), so you'll need to grab one from the nearby pool of fish. This will give you an unusual trout and give this trout to Offalfoot. He'll give you the shard. Note: You do need a fishing rod (the highest level is recommended) and this can be done with level 1 Fishing. You will encounter Delrom when traversing to through this location.

Current cycle of the universe begins

The Elder Gods shape the known universe after destroying the last one from the previous cycle, in an event known as the Great Revision. They eventually created Gielinor, their perfect world. Bik, Ful, and Wen laid their eggs deep within it, so that the anima the world produced would feed them. Jas had no egg to lay, having sacrificed hers to create the Stone of Jas. The dragonkin, a race of winged, reptile-like creatures, would survive the Great Revision by hiding in the Abyss.
They noticed that some anima created tasted different, thus they turned a continent of the planet into a vent for the anima, which would create an event known as the Anima Twist.
The servitors of the Elder Gods

When the Elder Gods settled upon Gielinor, they brought the TokHaar, servants of the Elders, who were tools of the The Elder Kiln that helped forge the world. Some would be moved to Ashenfall in order to safeguard the Lens, a tool that was made to ensure the sun's light would be in a perfect temperature for the world. They would later be known as the KotHaar.

After millennia of searching for a new suitable homeworld, the dragonkin would land on Gielinor and found Orthen (which translates to "first city") on what is now Anachronia. The dragonkin researched and documented the world's native flora and fauna.

A particular dragonkin by the name of Kerapac creates the Crucible, a device capable of converting normal anima into shadow anima, which he claims can bring their society equal in power to that of the Elder Gods. Without the approval of the other dragonkin, Kerapac uses this dangerous device, transforming vast quantities of anima. This angers the Elder Gods and, in response, Jas would destroy Orthen and enslave the dragonkin to the Stone of Jas.

Bound to the Stone as its guardians, the dragonkin were made to feel the pain of its misuse and were driven to hunt down any who were not an Elder God that drew power from it. The binding could not be undone, and the factions of Orthen each turned to a different means of escaping it. Kerapac's own Dactyl answered with science and created the dragons, hoping for a line beyond Jas's reach. The Nodon chose instead to sleep, entering a shared dream to wait the curse out. The Aughra left their bodies behind altogether, projecting their consciousness into other forms. The Necrosyrtes gave themselves over to the curse and took up the hunt as their purpose.

After travelling through the cosmos, Guthix discovered Gielinor and filled the world with new inhabitants. He also found several elder artefacts, tools used by the Elder Gods. He would discover Ashenfall and the unique properties of the continent with some of his followers, making a settlement in Brynmoor.

During Guthix's stay in Ashenfall, he discovered magical rocks, researching, and studying them to try to get them to harness the element of the world, thus creating the first runes after using the Stone of Jas for help.

Guthix would depart from Ashenfall to spread his discovery to the rest of the inhabitants he brought with him. Those who followed him to Ashenfall would remain and start forming settlements. The first being Bramblemead Village, which was founded by Guthix when Ashenfall was discovered. Some humans would form the Wild Knights, an order of skilled scouts who protect the people from the wild.

As the humans grew to inhabit their new homes, several would change in appearance, with beards turning into leaves, skin glowing like fire, and some even transforming to take on the qualities of the elements, thus gaining elemental abilities and becoming Amalgamated humans. Some humans would see them as impure or imperfect, where they would treat the Amalgamated humans differently, where the Amalgamated humans would suffer persecution and even be murdered by those who feared them. The Wild Knights and some other humans would attempt to protect the Amalgamated humans, offering them refuge against those who hunted them down.

Guthix would return to Ashenfall, where he would witness, in horror, the crimes some of his followers committed. He would take some of the humans with him to the mainland- those who did not join the rest in killing the Amalgamated- and leave those who murdered the Amalgamated in Ashenfall. He would then appoint the Wild Knights as protectors of Ashenfall, to safeguard the wilds from the settlers and the settlers from the wilds. Guthix would attempt to hide Ashenfall from the rest of the world, placing a veil over the continent in the hope that it would not be discovered. Guthix would then hide from the world and go into a deep sleep, in the hope that he would be forgotten.

Despite the veil being placed, a group of dragonkin, who were fleeing persecution known as the Cabal would discover Ashenfall and settle within the northern region of Ashenfall, where they would use the continent's anima to create a new settlement for themselves. They would spread across Ashenfall, creating Vaults to commence different experiments.
The garou would arrive on Gielinor, led by their goddess Lougrim and settled in the mainland

On the mainland, a different continent, more gods would begin to arrive on Gielinor, causing minor conflicts over land and followers. Different gods would arrive, and others would ascend within Gielinor, each one claiming a large amount of land and followers. The Kharidian - Zarosian War would be a major point in history, ending with the betrayal of the Mahjarrat and the Zarosian Empire as the victor.

Late in the Second Age, the Mahjarrat Zamorak turned on his master. Using two of the elder artefacts, he betrayed Zaros and drained away enough of his power to ascend as a god in his own right, leaving Zaros presumed defeated and vanished into the void. News of the usurpation spread across Gielinor, and it was that news which began the God Wars.

Years after the defeat of Zaros by the hand of Zamorak, Zamorak returned from his departure to reclaim the Stone of Jas The mainland would be in a global conflict, with Zamorak fighting against Saradomin, Armadyl, and sometimes Bandos. Other gods and/or their followers participated in the war to claim land or power; some allied with one another. Civilians would flee the mainland in search of a new place to live in, not tainted by war. Amongst them are the garou, leg by lougrim

During the God Wars, Saradominist missionaries would arrive on the continent in hopes of escaping the ongoing war on the mainland. They would be welcomed and eventually start converting the Guthixians to worship Saradomin. Sometime later, the Runecrafting Guild was built to allow the Saradominist wizards a place of study and magical research. The Temple of Saradomin was later built as a house of worship. The Adventurer's Guild was formed to train new adventurers. The Bronze Advisors, an alliance between the Saradominists and Guthixians, would be formed to oversee equality between both religious beliefs. Some Zamorakians, who travelled with the Saradominist refugees in secret, would form the Children of Shadows. Lougrim would escape the mainland with the garou, settling within Ghornfell.

The Saradominists would seek to become the dominant influence in Bramblemead, overthrowing the Guthixian druids and pushing them elsewhere on the continent. Policies began to slip more and more in favour of the Saradominist approach as the Guthixian faith slowly dwindled. The settlement of Bramblemead would begin to be ruled by a lord. The Keep of Blue Flames would be built for the lord to watch over the settlement. The Knights of Saradomin were formed as official police and army forces for Bramblemead. The Rasmodels would be exiled from Brynmoor, forcing them to travel further into the continent to make a home within Dowdun Reach. The Children of Shadows would follow along as their guards, later being reformed as the Black Knights.

The humans would soon deplete all of the iron within Bramblemead Valley and encroach into the northern regions in search of more iron. Some garou hunting parties would see this as disrespectful, and small skirmishes between the two took place. After the death of their prince, the Human-Garou War commenced. It mostly led to a stalemate, as the Whispering Swamp acted as a barrier between Brynmoor and the northern region.

The humans were forced to make a deal with the goblins for the assistance of the Bandosian army, with Bandos himself arriving to oversee the war in an attempt to face Lougrim, with whom he had a history. The garou would be pushed back, forcing Lougrim to make a deal with the dragonkin to tip the outcome in her favour. The dragonkin would unleash their dragons to attack the humans and their Bandosian allies. Bandos would personally intervene and face Velgar. Despite nearly winning, Bandos would be bested due to his arrogance, forcing the god of war to retreat. Velgar spilled his toxic blood on the fertile fields to the east, and this created the Bloodblight Swamp The Human loss would allow Lougrim to show mercy, forcing an uneasy alliance between the humans and garou. Kuldra would be created later on thanks to Lougrim's blood.

After the conflict, some human settlers would move to Fellhollow, to get away from the conflict the garou and humans were still committing. They founded Emberwood village. The ogres would arrive and live in harmony with the human settlers there. Imaru and Xikotal would be discovered by the settlers, but would be protected by the dragons, who assisted them in growing their crops and defending them from stray dragons. Within Dowdun Reach, the Black Knights would continue their rule, enslaving goblins and welcoming refugees, ensuring they worked as well.

Years after Kuldra's creation, she assembled an army to overthrow the dragonkin. The dragonkin would start dying out, leaving Kuldra to be titled Dragon Queen. Lougrim and Kuldra would later fight, causing the Fractured Plains to be formed in Ghornfell. Kuldra would ambush Lougrim and devour her. Kuldra becomes the High Queen; some of the garou reject her claim due to her victory being dishonourable. These factions would move to Umbral Sands.

The garou living here would struggle, as they were not used to living in a sandy region. They would discover Elidinis, who had arrived in the region at an unknown point in time. She began to teach the garou how to live in the region. She would soon be worshipped by them after her followers on the mainland learned she was associated with the moon. Cities would be made, allowing them to live in much better conditions Elidinis would later leave Gielinor.

After overthrowing their masters and devouring Lougrim, Kuldra would order her children and the dragons to attack the human settlements. Imaru and Xikotal showed mercy to the humans, which was a direct affront to Kuldra's orders. Xikotal would be killed by Kuldra as punishment, leaving Imaru and the humans in Emberwood to grieve. Velgar would lay waste to Brynmoor's settlement, ruling it and Ghornfell. Fuzan would rule over Umbral Sands, where he would terrorise the garou there. After hearing of the dragon's attack, the Black Knights would defend the keep against invading dragons.

Imaru would seek Ravanna to revive her beloved; instead, she is gifted with more power, a curse. Imaru would attempt to use this against Kuldra, only to be killed by the God-Eater. Imaru would drink from the River Noumenon and claw her way out from death to continue her fight against Kuldra. Instead, she is corrupted and becomes hungry for souls. Due to the spreading rot and corruption of Imaru, inhabitants of Fellhollow would slowly turn into undead. Ravanna, unwilling to see the whole of Ashenfall and the greater world of Gielinor fall to Imaru's hunger, would split Imaru's curse into three fragments and seal the undead dragon in her tower.

After hearing of Imaru's death, the Black Knights were ordered to spare any blue dragon, believing it could preserve balance. The Wither plague within Fellhollow would cause the knights to close and block the access that linked the two regions. Guards were stationed in the crypt and graveyard to ensure undead would not rise due to the plague. Eventually, the Dreaming Stone, a crystal discovered by the knights, would start spreading whispers amongst them. Madness would start, and with the Dreaming Stone destroyed, it lingered for centuries.

Fuzan rules over Umbral Sands and attacks the garou there. He would speak to an entity who claims she was a god from off-world, a queen, and promised Fuzan power that could outshine even his mother. He accepts and begins to worship her. Fuzan learned to better wield his flames and other flames, and to mark the souls of his victims to empower himself and the goddess. Fuzan would take control of the KotHaar and the Lens, rendering the region uninhabitable during the day. The Entity would gather followers among the garou, either by transforming them or by having them worship the sun or flames. Fuzan would continue to terrorize the garou in Umbral Sands for fun.

On the mainland, an alliance of Saradomin, Bandos, and Armadyl pushed Zamorak to the brink of defeat. In a last desperate ploy he used the Stone of Jas to set off a blast that wiped the region of Forinthry from the map, leaving behind the Wilderness in its place. Aside from whole settlements of aviansie, an army of them was reduced to ash in the same moment, among them Armadyl's own husband. The devastation was enough to wake Guthix from his slumber.
Guthix would awaken and end the gods' war using the Edicts to place a barrier around Gielinor, evicting the gods and ensuring none enters Gielinor, only the demigods and powerful beings would remain.

Ashenfall remains hidden within the veil. Any survivors who fled would lose their memories of it. Some travellers would encounter Ashenfall and either die there or leave, but could never spread the knowledge of it. Gielinor as a whole would slowly recover from the God Wars, rediscovering Runecrafting, teleportation, and more.

Guthix's resting place was discovered, alerting all of the gods' followers who wished for their respective god to return. The Guardians of Guthix would arrive, and with the assistance of the Adventurer The adventurer is made a new guardian. Guthix was slain by the Mahjarrat Sliske The adventurer is titled the World Guardian, with the power to protect Gielinor.

With Guthix dead and his Edicts undone, the gods returned to Gielinor and the world fell into conflict once more. Zamorak and Saradomin were the first to fight, attempting to claim Guthix's energy found in Lumbridge. Zamorak was defeated. A contest for the Stone of Jas was issued by Sliske, with the winner needing to be the one who kills the most gods. Bandos would participate and build a weapon to kill a god. Armadyl would do the same in order to prevent Bandos from using the weapon. Bandos was defeated and killed. Zaros returned. Brassica Prime and Marimbo would have their own "conflict", a party contest, where Brassica was the winner. Tuska started making her way to Gielinor. Most of the world's factions joined forces to stop her. The Godless is victorious in dealing the most damage. She is slain by Vorago, who allied with the Godless. Seren returned. The Heart of Gielinor is found, and a battle has started between Zarosians, Serenists, Zamorakians, and Sliske's followers. Sliske's contest ends, with the stone being destroyed. A council is formed to deal with a new threat: the Elder Gods. Zaros would leave this universe, entering Erebus. Elder Gods' eggs are close to hatching. The eggs are moved to a secure location, and the remaining gods would assist in harnessing the anima within them to delay the hatching. A battle was started between the Elder Gods and the mortals of Gielinor. The battle concluded with Jas being sealed in Erebus and the eggs being hatched in Iaia, where they remain with Seren. Zamorak would invade Gielinor with his army of demons and followers. The world factions once again joined forces to defend the civilians. The World Guardian and the Guardians of Guthix learn how to recreate the Edicts of Guthix. The World Guardian, with help, fought Zamorak and banished him from Gielinor. Eventually, all other gods are banished as well, even those who are considered as powerful as gods, such as Nex. Gielinor, once again, is in the hands of mortals.

After the turmoil on the mainland, Ashenfall was revealed, and many rich individuals funded an expedition to discover more about this mysterious land. This expedition would find the continent of Ashenfall ruled by dragons, and many members would die in dragon attacks. Only the Wise Old Man, the leader of the expedition, Vannaka, Zanik, Doric, and a young adventurer called Cathan would be among the survivors of the attacks who'd wash up upon the shores of Ashenfall.

Traversing through the wilderness of Ashenfall, the remaining survivors would discover an old Saradominist church ravaged by time's decay. They would uncover an inactive lodestone in the church and, using supplies they found on their travels, repair it to contact the mainland. While waiting for reinforcements from the mainland, the young adventurer Cathan would leave the group to set off on his own to defeat the dragon overlords.

With contact established with the mainland, many adventurers teleport into the ruined Saradominist temple to meet with the Wise Old Man and learn the basics of surviving in this strange continent. Once these adventurers get their bearings, they report to the Wise Old Man, who sends them out to look for Cathan. They eventually find his ghost lingering near his skeleton near Velgar's Rise in Ghornfell, who tells them about making a horn to challenge Velgar. They defeat Velgar and open the way to Fellhollow and to put to rest the revenant dragoness Imaru at the behest of Death. After putting Imaru to her final rest, handing her head to Death, they head to the ominous gateway to meet up with the Wise Old Man once more to uncover the secrets of the Dreaming Stone (later revealed to be a dragonkin called Avisk) and open the way to the Umbral Sands. When the way opened to the desert, defeating the Black Knight Titan, they ventured forth to meet with Icthlarin and build a reputation with the Moon Garou to overthrow the tyrant Fuzan. With Fuzan defeated, the only threat left was his mother, Kuldra.
